name: Dipankar Chatterjee
current_role: Whole-time director (listed as chairman by some sources), Luxmi Tea Co. Pvt Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Son of Paresh Chandra Chatterjee, who founded Luxmi Tea in Kolkata in 1912 as a swadeshi venture. Dipankar took over the business in the 1980s and grew it into one of India's larger tea groups (Assam, Darjeeling, Tripura and African estates, incl. Makaibari, bought 2014). His son Rudra Chatterjee is now managing director.
interesting_fact: Luxmi Tea was founded in 1912 by his father as a protest against British colonial rule; today the group produces tea from ~25 estates in India and Africa and owns Darjeeling's famed Makaibari estate.
deep_cut_fact: After buying Assam's Narayanpur Tea Estate, he noticed its tea was popular with buyers from Rajasthan and created a 'Narayanpur Tea' sub-brand, described as probably the first Indian tea brand named after a region.
notes: Low public profile; son Rudra Chatterjee (MD) is the group's public face and a frequent speaker, likely the best route. Alive status not confirmed by recent news.

name: Lou Xiaoqiang
current_role: Co-founder, President & COO of Pharmaron; CEO of Pharmaron Clinical
profile: Lou Xiaoqiang (Larry Lou) co-founded Beijing-based contract research/manufacturing group Pharmaron in 2004 with his brother Boliang Lou (chairman/CEO) and Zheng Bei. Pharmaron is listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong and serves global drugmakers with labs in China, the US and UK. He runs operations and the clinical services arm.
interesting_fact: Pharmaron grew from a Beijing chemistry lab founded in 2004 into a fully integrated R&D services platform with sites in China, the US and the UK, listed in both Shenzhen and Hong Kong.
deep_cut_fact: Before Pharmaron he was a tech entrepreneur: he founded and ran Beijing Biopass Technology, an information-security product company. He trained as a materials scientist (BS/MS, Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) and holds a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: bd@ is the company's general/business-development address, not a dedicated press line. Fortune shared with Zheng Bei (co-founder). Brother Boliang Lou is chairman/CEO and the more public figure.

name: Richard Teets Jr
current_role: Co-founder and former director of Steel Dynamics (retired from board May 2026; retired as President/COO of Steel Operations 2016)
profile: Mechanical engineer Richard 'Dick' Teets left Nucor with Keith Busse and Mark Millett to co-found Fort Wayne-based Steel Dynamics in 1993, taking it public in 1996. He ran its steelmaking divisions as EVP and President/COO of Steel Operations until 2016, then served on the board until May 2026. He holds roughly 3% of the company.
interesting_fact: Steel Dynamics, which he co-founded in 1993 as an electric-arc-furnace mini-mill startup, became one of the largest US steel producers and metals recyclers.
deep_cut_fact: He began in the late 1970s as a mechanical engineer at J&L Steel and at Nucor supervised construction of the first thin-cast slab steel plant; he is a past AIST president, received AIME Honorary Membership (2017) and the SMA's Iverson-Selig Award, and helped set up AIST Foundation scholarships.
notes: Retired from all Steel Dynamics roles as of May 2026; company IR is only an indirect route. Active in AIST (Association for Iron & Steel Technology) circles.

name: Hongbin Sun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sunac China Holdings (HKEX: 1918), Tianjin/Beijing
profile: Sun Hongbin (b. 1963, Shanxi) worked at Legend (Lenovo) before founding Tianjin property agency-turned-developer Shunchi (Sunco) in 1994 and Sunac in 2003, which became one of China's largest developers and bought Wanda's theme-park and hotel assets in 2017. Since 2022 he has steered Sunac through an offshore/onshore debt restructuring and remains chairman in 2026; his stake has been diluted.
interesting_fact: In 2017 Sunac bought a portfolio of cultural-tourism projects and hotels from Wang Jianlin's Wanda Group, pushing a homebuilder into theme parks and hotels.
deep_cut_fact: Before property he trained as an engineer in the power sector: he graduated from the Wuhan Water Conservancy and Electric Power College (now part of Wuhan University) in 1981 and earned a Tsinghua master's in engineering in 1985.
notes: US citizen based in Tianjin. Sunac is in post-default restructuring; avoid financial-distress framing. No dedicated published IR email found on sunac.com.cn (ESG reports list esg@sunac.com.cn). Background includes a 1990s conviction—avoid in outreach.

name: Edgar Sia II
profile: Edgar 'Injap' Sia II, an Iloilo-born architecture dropout, opened the first Mang Inasal grill restaurant in 2003 at 26 and sold it to Jollibee (Tony Tan Caktiong) in 2010-2016. With Tan Caktiong he built DoubleDragon (listed 2014), now an investment holding firm spanning CityMalls, Hotel101 (incl. Madrid, opened 2026) and MerryMart groceries; he targets P500bn revenue by 2035.
interesting_fact: DoubleDragon's Hotel101 opened a 680-room property in Madrid in March 2026, part of Sia's plan to take the Filipino condotel brand global.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he won a Honda Civic in a nationwide 'Text Challenge' by texting all day and paying a jobless college classmate P200/day to text overnight (with 3 a.m. wake-up calls); he sold the car and within a year opened the first Mang Inasal in an Iloilo mall carpark.
notes: Media-friendly and frequently interviewed by Philippine business press; nicknamed the 'promdi billionaire' (provincial).

name: Juan Fernando Belmont Anderson
current_role: Founder of Yanbal International (Peruvian direct-sales cosmetics); handed CEO role to daughter Janine Belmont in 2011
profile: Fernando Belmont Anderson founded Yanbal in Lima in 1967 after joining his father's Botica Francesa, the Peruvian Helena Rubinstein franchisee, and deciding to make cosmetics locally and sell them direct. He and brother Eduardo (later Belcorp founder) split their interests in 1988; Fernando took Yanbal into Spain and much of Latin America. He stepped back at 70 in 2011.
interesting_fact: He and his brother Eduardo started out together in Yanbal, then split in 1988 and became direct competitors, each building a billion-dollar door-to-door cosmetics company (Yanbal and Belcorp).
deep_cut_fact: Yanbal's model came from a problem at his father's Helena Rubinstein franchise: imports were too pricey for Peruvians, so he studied leading beauty brands and adopted local manufacturing plus the 'party plan' of home sales gatherings. The Yanbal name was inspired by his daughter Janine.
notes: Forbes lists him as 'Juan Fernando'; usually known as Fernando Belmont. Born c.1941; no death report found but no recent public activity either. Very private; daughter Janine Belmont (Yanbal CEO) is the public face. Last on Forbes list 2014.
